core_functions.description: ManX catalyzes the EIIAB phosphoryl relay from HPr through His10 and His175 to transported sugar in the assembled ManXYZ system. Transfer is possible both within one ManX polypeptide and between dimer subunits; membrane partners are required for coupled sugar transport and phosphorylation.

supported_by.supporting_text: In the presence of the IIMan subunits, the phosphoryl group is directly transferred from His-175 of P20 to the sugar substrates of the permease.
Phosphoryltransfer occurs not only between P13 and P20 on the same IIIMan subunit but also between isolated domains and between domains on different subunits of the dimer.

core_functions.description: ManY contributes the substrate-binding and membrane-translocation machinery of the assembled ManXYZ transporter. The ManYZ structure and counterflow assay establish direct transport work; ManX provides the sugar-phosphorylation chemistry. This core does not assign autonomous histidyl phosphotransfer to ManY.

supported_by.supporting_text: CoreY and CoreZ clamp the substrate to form the Core domain
All three subunits are required for sugar transport and phosphorylation
